concepts.note: Cauchy's 1822 stress principle represents surface traction as a tensor, which yields the viscous term μ∇²u in the momentum equation.
concepts.title: Cauchy stress tensor

concepts.note: When inertia is negligible the equations linearize, giving Stokes flow and the drag law F = 6πμRv for a sphere (1851).
concepts.title: Stokes flow and drag

concepts.note: Matching fluid velocity to solid walls closes the boundary-value problem, though slip appears in rarefied, microfluidic and superhydrophobic regimes.
concepts.title: No-slip boundary condition

concepts.note: Whether smooth three-dimensional solutions exist for all time and all smooth data is an unsolved Clay Millennium Prize problem (2000).
concepts.title: Existence and smoothness (open)

subtopics.note: These equations express momentum balance for a viscous Newtonian fluid, combining inertia with pressure and viscous stress: ρ(∂u/∂t + u·∇u) = −∇p + μ∇²u + f, with ∇·u = 0 for incompressible flow. Navier (1822) and Stokes (1845) introduced the viscous term through Cauchy's stress tensor.
subtopics.title: Navier-Stokes equations

concepts.note: Reynolds' 1883 pipe experiments showed laminar flow gives way to turbulence near Re = ρUL/μ ≈ 2000.
concepts.title: Reynolds number

concepts.note: Kolmogorov's similarity hypotheses (1941) give E(k) ∝ k^(−5/3) and the exact four-fifths law for third-order structure functions.
concepts.title: Kolmogorov −5/3 spectrum

concepts.note: Prandtl (1904) showed viscous effects confine to thin layers near walls, reconciling ideal-flow theory with observed drag and separation.
concepts.title: Boundary-layer theory

concepts.note: Averaging the equations generates unknown velocity correlations, so RANS and large-eddy models remain partly empirical — an open modeling question.
concepts.title: Closure problem

subtopics.note: Above a critical Reynolds number flow becomes chaotic and energy cascades from large eddies to small ones where viscosity dissipates it. Kolmogorov's 1941 theory predicts the inertial-range spectrum E(k) ∝ ε^(2/3) k^(−5/3).
subtopics.title: Turbulence

concepts.note: Debye and Hückel (1923) gave the screening length λ_D = √(ε₀kT/ne²), the scale over which a plasma neutralizes charge imbalances.
concepts.title: Debye shielding

concepts.note: Langmuir (1928) found collective electron oscillations at ω_p = √(ne²/ε₀m) and coined the term 'plasma' for the ionized state.
concepts.title: Plasma oscillations

concepts.note: Alfvén (1942) predicted transverse waves propagating along field lines at v_A = B/√(μ₀ρ), the cornerstone of MHD.
concepts.title: Alfvén waves

concepts.note: Field lines break and rejoin, releasing magnetic energy in solar flares and tokamak disruptions; the fast reconnection rate remains debated.
concepts.title: Magnetic reconnection

subtopics.note: In ionized gas, long-range Coulomb forces make particles act collectively over the Debye length, supporting waves and instabilities. Ideal magnetohydrodynamics couples fluid momentum to Maxwell's fields: ρ(∂u/∂t + u·∇u) = J×B − ∇p with ∂B/∂t = ∇×(u×B).
subtopics.title: Plasma physics and MHD

concepts.note: A positive Lyapunov exponent makes small errors grow as δ(t) ≈ δ₀e^(λt), setting a finite predictability horizon.
concepts.title: Sensitive dependence

concepts.note: Lorenz's 1963 three-variable convection equations produce a strange attractor of fractal geometry, popularized as the butterfly effect.
concepts.title: Lorenz attractor

concepts.note: Poincaré's 1890 work on the three-body problem found intersecting stable and unstable manifolds, a geometric mechanism for chaos.
concepts.title: Homoclinic tangles

concepts.note: Kolmogorov (1954) with Arnold and Moser (1962-63) proved most invariant tori survive small perturbations, delimiting where chaos appears.
concepts.title: KAM theorem

subtopics.note: Nonlinear deterministic systems can display sensitive dependence on initial conditions, so nearby trajectories separate exponentially and long-term prediction fails. Poincaré found the geometry in the three-body problem (1890) and Lorenz exhibited it in a truncated convection model (1963).
subtopics.title: Chaos

concepts.note: John Scott Russell observed in 1834 a solitary water wave that traveled for miles without changing shape.
concepts.title: Wave of translation

concepts.note: Korteweg and de Vries (1895) derived u_t + u u_x + δ²u_xxx = 0, balancing nonlinearity against dispersion.
concepts.title: Korteweg-de Vries equation

concepts.note: Gardner, Greene, Kruskal and Miura (1967) solved KdV by mapping it to a linear scattering problem, revealing infinitely many conservation laws.
concepts.title: Inverse scattering transform

concepts.note: Hasegawa and Tappert (1973) predicted nonlinear Schrödinger solitons in optical fibers, now exploited in long-haul communications.
concepts.title: Optical solitons

subtopics.note: A soliton is a localized wave that survives collisions unchanged because nonlinear steepening exactly balances dispersion. Zabusky and Kruskal coined the name in 1965 while numerically studying the Korteweg–de Vries equation u_t + u u_x + δ² u_xxx = 0.
subtopics.title: Solitons

concepts.note: Flory (1941) and Huggins described polymer solutions and blends with a lattice free energy governed by the interaction parameter χ.
concepts.title: Flory-Huggins theory

concepts.note: de Gennes (1971) and Doi-Edwards (1978) model entangled chains sliding in a tube, giving τ ~ N³ stress relaxation.
concepts.title: Reptation and tube model

concepts.note: Onsager (1949) and de Gennes explained orientational order and its nematic-isotropic transitions in rod-like and molecular materials.
concepts.title: Liquid crystals

concepts.note: Optical tweezers, FRET and cryo-EM since the 1990s measure forces and conformational changes in individual proteins, DNA and molecular motors.
concepts.title: Single-molecule biophysics

subtopics.note: Soft matter is governed by thermal energy kT and entropy, so weak interactions and Brownian motion set mesoscopic structure. Canonical results include polymer scaling R_F ~ N^(3/5)a and reptation dynamics with relaxation time τ ~ N³.
subtopics.title: Soft matter and biophysics

concepts.note: Bak, Tang and Wiesenfeld (1987) showed a cellular-automaton sandpile drives itself to a critical slope with power-law avalanche sizes.
concepts.title: Sandpile model

concepts.note: Critical states generate scale-free fluctuations, linking earthquakes, forest fires and neuronal avalanches to a common statistical signature.
concepts.title: 1/f noise and power laws

concepts.note: Watts and Strogatz (1998) found that a few random rewires sharply reduce path length while preserving high clustering.
concepts.title: Small-world networks

concepts.note: Extending the period, Barabási and Albert (1999) showed preferential attachment yields P(k) ~ k^(−3), so a few hubs dominate robustness and spreading.
concepts.title: Scale-free networks

subtopics.note: Slowly driven dissipative systems can organize themselves into a critical state without external tuning, yielding power-law avalanche statistics P(s) ~ s^(−τ). Network science then showed that topology, from small-world to scale-free structure, controls collective behaviour.
subtopics.title: Self-organized criticality and networks
